method: one separate process per phase over the same deterministic corpus; each phase object is embedded verbatim from the gated harness

decode.method: TIME-COMPRESSED machine-9 endurance: one process sustaining a deterministic mixed read (decode) / write (publish) / append (non-withdrawal) workload over 20,000 x 100-byte records shared through a trained OrANS-DICT dictionary; a counting global allocator reports live bytes and counts, RSS/VmHWM come from /proc/self/status via ekbloom::current_rss_bytes / peak_rss_bytes; every batch pushes a time-series sample
decode.caveat: This is a TIME-COMPRESSED run, not a 7-day run. The operation scheduling is deterministic from the seed regardless of the budget (only the count varies with wall-clock), but the absolute rates and the 7-day decode-operation count are host-dependent and are an operation-count projection only: they do not model sustained filesystem growth, allocator arena retention, page-cache pressure, or thermal/clock drift over days.

decode_latency.sample_rule: per-decode-op latency, one time-ordered uniform sample capped at 2^18 entries (each time the cap is hit, every other sample is dropped and the stride doubles, preserving the first and last regions); first_decile = the first 10% of the sample by time, last_decile = the last 10% by time; p50/p99 from ekbloom::percentiles, p99_9 by the same nearest-rank definition

memory.plateau_rule: plateau = (max RSS over the second half of samples - max RSS over the first half) < 5% of the first-half max
memory.rss_creep_rule: rss_creep_bytes_per_s_last_half = least-squares slope of rss_bytes against time over the second half of the time-uniform sample (B/s); rss_creep_7day_bytes = max(0, slope) * 604800, an operation-count-style projection ONLY. The live-memory leak test is alloc_live_flat: the second-half live-byte range must be <= 1% of its second-half max (a bounded sawtooth counts as flat, which a 'never changes again' test would wrongly reject); alloc_end_equals_max and alloc_flat_after_ms are reported alongside

decode.fragmentation_method: alloc_in_use is what the counting global allocator holds live; rss_bytes is the kernel resident set (VmRSS) read from /proc/self/status; rss_minus_in_use_max = rss_max - alloc_in_use_max is the non-allocator resident proxy (stacks, code, page tables, allocator metadata and retained arenas); leak_bytes = alloc_in_use_end - alloc_in_use_at_end_of_first_cycle; rss_drift_bytes = last RSS - RSS at end of the first cycle (after warmup); alloc_flat_after_ms = the first sampled time after which in_use_bytes never changes again (the exact live-memory plateau); alloc_end_equals_max = in_use_end == alloc_in_use_max
